requests.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: authored 16-cel whole-body animation sheet for a modern battlefield game.
Input image 1: EDIT TARGET, the supplied infantry-stance-v142.png. Edit this existing sheet; it is the authority for character identity, anatomy, rendering, pose sequence, and camera.
Output: exactly ONE square PNG sheet, preferably 2048x2048, with genuine transparent alpha. Empty space must have alpha zero, not painted black, white, gray, or checkerboard.
Composition: exactly sixteen separate full-body cels in four rows and four columns, read left to right then top to bottom. Match all sixteen source poses one for one: standing through lowering and kneeling, forward descent, and the four final prone stages. Preserve the source's exact whole-body progression, adult body proportions, detailed painted realistic olive uniform, helmet, vest, pouches, boots, face, lighting, RIGHT-facing side view, camera angle, and consistent character scale. Preserve planted foot/knee/elbow contact relationships and source pose baselines. Do not replace intermediate cels with repeated endpoint poses.
Edit boundaries: change the weapon and only the local hand/forearm positioning needed for a plausible grip on that weapon. Preserve the rest of each body pose; no new gestures. Every cel must visibly retain the SAME specified weapon at the SAME physical scale, including all transitional and prone cels.
Spacing: generous fully transparent separation between all sixteen complete silhouettes and around the sheet. Entire weapon, muzzle, stock or rear tube, bipod, helmet, hands and both boots must fit visibly without touching neighboring cels or the image border. No cropping, overlap, connected silhouettes, or miniature weapons used to fake fit.
Scene/backdrop: none. Ground contact refers only to an implied invisible baseline; do not draw a ground surface.
Avoid: hand signals, raised arms, waving, ladders, climbing, extra limbs, extra weapons, captions, lettering, frame numbers, grid lines, panel borders, ground, cast shadows, backdrop, muzzle flash, or decorative effects.
Weapon replacement: In ALL SIXTEEN cels replace the assault rifle completely with one clearly recognizable belt-fed compact LIGHT MACHINE GUN. Keep the same robust receiver, visible ammunition belt feeding from an ammunition box/box magazine UNDER the receiver, sturdy longer barrel, and folded bipod along that barrel throughout the sequence. Its silhouette must read as an LMG in every cel, never as the original assault rifle. Both hands maintain plausible rear grip and forward support throughout the posture transition. In the final bottom-right prone cel the LMG barrel/bipod assembly is supported at the invisible ground baseline, with the bipod deployed naturally for support. The soldier remains attached to and operating this portable weapon; NO stationary gun, NO tripod mount. Preserve all sixteen reference body poses and the whole original soldier design.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: authored whole-body game animation atlas, supplemental LOWERING choreography.
Primary request: Create ONE NEW PNG atlas containing exactly TWENTY-FOUR independent full-body soldier figures. This is a new knees-to-prone animation asset with three weapon-specific eight-frame chains. It is not an edit or reproduction of an earlier sheet.
Output and alpha: Prefer 2048x3072 pixels, 2:3 PORTRAIT. Exactly FOUR columns by SIX rows, twenty-four equal invisible square cells. Genuine transparent RGBA background, with fully empty alpha-zero space between all figures and around all borders. No painted black, white, gray, or checkerboard background.
Character and finish: Detailed painted realistic adult soldier seen strictly SIDE-ON facing RIGHT in every cel. Realistic human anatomy and proportions, muted olive combat uniform, olive helmet, tactical vest and pouches, gloves, knee protection and dark boots. Weathered fabric and metal, the restrained realistic material finish of the previously shown olive infantry reference. Clear authored silhouettes and small painted detail, never blocky pixel-art anatomy, never a cartoon or toy. Same adult identity, equipment, body proportions, camera, lighting and body scale throughout all 24 cels.
CRITICAL SCALE AND ISOLATION: Use a deliberately SMALL soldier scale and keep it identical in EVERY cel, including kneeling and prone. Do not zoom, crop, or enlarge low/prone figures to fill space. The ENTIRE combined body-plus-weapon silhouette, including both boots, helmet, tube rear, muzzle, suppressor, belt box, and bipod, must remain strictly inside the CENTRAL 78% of each cell's WIDTH, with at least 11% fully transparent horizontal margin on BOTH sides. The longest prone body-plus-weapon must occupy no more than 240 pixels in an approximately 320-wide cell at about 1254-pixel atlas width; equivalently no more than about 392 pixels in a 512-wide cell at 2048-pixel atlas width. Kneeling body height should be about 140 pixels and prone body height about 55 pixels at 1254-wide output, or about 229 and 90 pixels respectively at 2048-wide output. Maintain this shared anatomical scale instead of resizing individual poses or shortening weapons. Generous empty transparent space is intentional and essential. All ground-contact points align to the same invisible baseline at 84% of each cell's height. No part may touch a neighbor, cell edge, or atlas edge.
Layout and reading order:
TOP TWO ROWS, cells 1-8: the SAME portable belt-fed LIGHT MACHINE GUNNER lowering through eight consecutive poses. Recognizable belt feed, ammunition box beneath the receiver, sturdy barrel and bipod. Keep the same LMG visible in every frame; it never becomes an assault rifle or a stationary tripod gun.
MIDDLE TWO ROWS, cells 9-16: the SAME shoulder-fired RPG GUNNER lowering through the same eight stages. Long olive shoulder tube extending visibly behind the shoulder and forward, shoulder rest, and distinct bulged front rocket warhead pointing right. Keep the whole tube and warhead visible and at the same physical size in every frame, including prone. No additional rifle.
BOTTOM TWO ROWS, cells 17-24: the SAME SNIPER lowering through the same eight stages. Long precision rifle with obvious scope, slim suppressed barrel and bipod. Keep the scope and suppressor distinct and the same weapon visible throughout.
For EACH weapon's eight-frame chain, read left-to-right across its first row and then left-to-right across its second row. Match these exact stages:
Frame 0: firmly kneeling on one knee, other foot planted, gun forward.
Frame 1: chest leans forward while still kneeling.
Frame 2: free support hand plants on the invisible ground baseline to bear weight; other hand keeps the weapon visibly controlled.
Frame 3: torso lowers further and rear leg extends back.
Frame 4: both legs extend, pelvis drops low, torso approaches prone.
Frame 5: belly and elbows settle into prone support.
Frame 6: small but visible elbow repositioning and aim adjustment in low prone.
Frame 7: steady fully prone aiming RIGHT.
All eight poses must be visibly distinct, gradual, and anatomically plausible. Preserve continuous limb and weapon identity. The support hand may briefly leave the weapon to support body weight during frames 2-4, then return to a plausible firing grip. In the prone endpoint, LMG/sniper bipods can support their weapons at the invisible baseline, and the RPG remains supported low and fully visible.
Avoid: neighboring silhouettes touching or overlapping; clipped boots, barrel, suppressor or launcher; scale changes; oversized prone figures; duplicated poses; missing or changing weapons; extra figures or limbs; command gestures, raised arms, waving, ladders or climbing; text, labels, numbers, captions, grid, cell outlines, background, ground surface, cast shadows, muzzle flash or decorative effects. Produce only this single transparent 24-cel atlas.
